question.text: Five identical capacitors, of capacitance $20 \mu \mathrm{F}$ each, are connected to a battery of $150 \mathrm{V}$, in a combination as shown in the diagram. What is the total amount of charge stored?

solution.text: The given circuit shows a balanced Wheatstone bridge. Now, the circuit becomes In the branch $A B,$ both capacitor are arranged in the series combination. Hence, its cquivalent capacitance is given by $$ \begin{array}{l} \frac{1}{C_{A B}}=\frac{1}{20}+\frac{1}{20}=\frac{2}{20}=\frac{1}{10} \\ C_{A B}=10 \mu \mathrm{F} \end{array} $$ Similarly, in branch $\mathrm{CD}$, $$ C_{C D}=10 \mu \mathrm{F} $$ Now, $C_{A B}$ and $C_{C D}$ are connected in parallel combination. Hence, the equivalent capacitance of the circuit, $$ C_{\mathrm{eq}}=10+10=20 \mu \mathrm{F} $$ We know that, charge $Q=C_{\mathrm{eq}} V$ $$ Q=20 \times 10^{-6} \times 150 \mathrm{V} $$ Amount of charge stored $Q=3 \times 10^{-3} C$
